title: Git & GitHub Development Workflow Core v2

domain.name: Git & GitHub Development Workflow
domain.description: Advanced Git and GitHub practice covering branching strategy, history surgery, reflog recovery, worktrees, review systems, CI, releases, and repository security. Provider-specific UI and current GitHub behavior belong in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Advanced Branching & Integration Strategy
competencies.description: Choose trunk, short-lived feature, release, and stabilization patterns based on team and delivery needs.
competencies.purpose: Reduce merge cost and history confusion while preserving review and rollback.

units.title: Branch strategy should minimize divergence
units.content: The longer branches diverge, the more integration risk grows; strategy should match release cadence, review needs, and ownership.

units.title: Integration planning workflow
units.content: Identify base and ownership, keep branches focused, fetch before integration, choose merge/rebase policy deliberately, validate combined behavior, and verify remote state after push.

units.title: Branch strategy failures
units.content: Avoid long-lived personal branches with hidden dependencies, mixing release and feature concerns, force-updating shared branches casually, and rebasing without checking downstream consumers.

drills.title: Choose a branch strategy for FREEOS
drills.prompt: Design a practical branching and integration strategy for rapid local development with frequent staged curriculum and operator features.

competencies.name: Rebase, Cherry-Pick & History Surgery
competencies.description: Rewrite unpublished history intentionally while preserving work and protecting collaborators.
competencies.purpose: Clean or transplant commits without accidental loss.

units.title: History rewriting changes commit identity
units.content: Rebase, amend, squash, and cherry-pick create new commit identities even when file content looks similar, which matters once others depend on old commits.

units.title: Safe history-rewrite workflow
units.content: Confirm branch ownership and push state, create a safety reference, inspect commit graph, perform the minimal rewrite, resolve conflicts by intent, run validation, compare before/after, and push with lease only when policy permits.

units.title: History-surgery failures
units.content: Avoid rewriting shared main history, using force push without lease, dropping commits because conflict resolution was rushed, and squashing away useful audit boundaries blindly.

drills.title: Clean unpublished history safely
drills.prompt: Plan an interactive rebase to reorder, squash, and edit several local commits while preserving a rollback point.

competencies.name: Bisect, Reflog & Advanced Recovery
competencies.description: Use binary search, reflog, detached commits, restore, revert, and reset choices to recover or locate regressions.
competencies.purpose: Find bad changes and rescue work with evidence instead of guessing.

units.title: Git often retains recoverable object history temporarily
units.content: Reflog can reveal previous branch and HEAD positions after resets, rebases, and detached work, but recovery should happen before cleanup or garbage collection removes reachability clues.

units.title: Recovery workflow
units.content: Stop destructive actions, inspect status/log/reflog, create a branch at valuable orphaned commits, choose revert for shared-history undo, use bisect with a repeatable test for regressions, and verify restored work before cleanup.

units.title: Recovery failure modes
units.content: Avoid repeated hard resets while confused, expiring reflog evidence through cleanup, bisecting with nondeterministic tests, and rewriting shared history when revert would be safer.

drills.title: Recover work after a mistaken reset
drills.prompt: Define exact inspection and recovery steps after a developer resets away several valuable local commits.

competencies.name: Worktrees & Parallel Repository Workflows
competencies.description: Use Git worktrees and repository boundaries to isolate simultaneous tasks without unsafe stash churn.
competencies.purpose: Support parallel development and autonomous task queues cleanly.

units.title: A worktree shares repository history but has its own working tree
units.content: Worktrees let different branches be checked out simultaneously while sharing object storage, which can reduce context switching and accidental mixed changes.

units.title: Worktree workflow
units.content: Choose a branch per task, create worktree in a deliberate location, verify clean status and build context, keep generated artifacts scoped, commit before integration, then remove the worktree only after work is preserved.

units.title: Worktree failure modes
units.content: Avoid pointing multiple tasks at the same output folders, deleting worktree directories manually before Git cleanup, editing shared external state unknowingly, and merging unfinished task branches blindly.

drills.title: Plan parallel FREEOS development with worktrees
drills.prompt: Design how two autonomous coding tasks could operate on separate branches/worktrees and reintegrate safely.

competencies.name: Pull Request Review Strategy
competencies.description: Review by risk, contract, behavior, tests, migrations, configuration, and rollback impact rather than line count alone.

units.title: Review depth should follow blast radius
units.content: Authentication, migrations, permissions, deployment, data loss, and public contracts deserve more scrutiny than isolated low-risk presentation changes.

units.title: Risk-based review workflow
units.content: Read intent and changed-file summary, identify high-blast-radius areas, inspect removed safeguards and config, trace behavior changes, map tests to risks, run or inspect evidence, and require rollback understanding before approval.

units.title: Review failures
units.content: Avoid reviewing only green CI, focusing on formatting while missing behavior, ignoring deleted code, trusting generated files without source changes, and approving changes whose rollback is unknown.

drills.title: Review a high-risk infrastructure PR
drills.prompt: Create a review checklist for a PR changing authentication, environment configuration, database migration, and deployment scripts.

competencies.name: GitHub Actions & CI Pipelines
competencies.description: Design deterministic CI workflows with least privilege, caching discipline, artifacts, matrices, and release gates.
competencies.purpose: Automate verification without granting workflows unnecessary power.

units.title: CI is privileged automation
units.content: Workflow triggers, tokens, third-party actions, secrets, artifacts, and write permissions create a supply-chain and repository-control boundary.

units.title: CI design workflow
units.content: Define trigger and required checks, pin trusted action versions, minimize token permissions, separate untrusted PR execution from secrets, cache only safe dependencies, capture artifacts/logs, and make release jobs require stronger gates.

units.title: CI failure modes
units.content: Avoid broad write permissions, exposing secrets to forked code, unpinned third-party actions, cache keys that restore incompatible state, and deployment from unreviewed branches.

drills.title: Design a secure FREEOS CI workflow
drills.prompt: Plan build, test, artifact, and optional release jobs for FREEOS with minimal permissions.

competencies.name: Release Engineering, Tags & Versioning
competencies.description: Create traceable releases with immutable source references, changelogs, artifacts, verification, and rollback.
competencies.purpose: Know exactly what was delivered and how to recover.

units.title: A version should identify a reproducible state
units.content: Source commit, dependencies, build configuration, artifact metadata, migration state, and release notes together define a useful release record.

units.title: Release workflow
units.content: Choose exact commit, confirm checks, update version/changelog, create signed or policy-approved tag where applicable, build once from that state, record artifact hashes, publish release notes, and preserve rollback instructions.

units.title: Release failures
units.content: Avoid moving release tags casually, rebuilding different binaries under the same version, releasing from a dirty working tree, and shipping without a rollback reference.

drills.title: Define a production release record
drills.prompt: Specify the evidence FREEOS should retain for a reproducible tagged release.

competencies.name: Repository Security & Dependency Hygiene
competencies.description: Protect secrets, dependency trust, branch policies, automation credentials, generated artifacts, and repository access boundaries.

units.title: Repository compromise can become runtime compromise
units.content: Dependencies, workflows, scripts, hooks, generated code, and release artifacts can execute with developer or CI privileges; review trust boundaries as code.

units.title: Repository-security workflow
units.content: Keep secrets out of Git, scan accidental exposures, review dependency/source provenance, minimize workflow permissions, inspect automation changes carefully, rotate exposed credentials first, and use branch/review policies proportional to risk.

units.title: Repository security failures
units.content: Avoid trusting lockfile changes without context, accepting secret deletion as credential remediation, running unknown repository scripts automatically, and granting CI broad write tokens for convenience.

drills.title: Audit a repository security boundary
drills.prompt: Review a repository for secret exposure, dependency risk, CI permissions, release integrity, and unsafe automation assumptions.
